checks.reason: can_have_body belongs to a family of separate HTTP predicates (can_have_body, can_chunked, can_have_content_length, can_have_implicit_zero_content_length). Whether a response may have a body and whether chunked transfer coding may be used are different questions that happen to agree today. can_chunked drives the transfer-encoding/trailer decisions, while can_have_body drives the 'force body to 0' rule, so calling can_chunked there would misstate the reason and couple two concepts that may diverge.
Pure forward to can_chunked, but it names a distinct concept (body allowed) used at a separate call site, plausibly a semantic alias that may diverge.
